result.title: Over-parameterization Is Neither Robust nor Fragile in Matrix Sensing: A Geometric Theory of Solution Robustness
result.summary: Over-parameterization is ubiquitous in modern machine learning, yet its effect on robustness remains poorly understood. We study this question in matrix sensing, a canonical non-convex problem that can also be viewed, under an appropriate parameterization, as training a two-layer quadratic neural network. We develop a rank-aware robustness theory for the Burer-Monteiro factorization when the search rank k may exceed the target rank r_star, thereby capturing over-parameterization. Our analysis shows that robustness depends jointly on the degree of over-parameterization and the local geometry of the attained second-order stationary point: increasing k generally worsens sensitivity, but stationary points with the same search rank can exhibit substantially different robustness. Motivated by this observation, we propose a trajectory-aware algorithm that uses spectral balancing and randomized sketching to steer optimization toward less sensitive solutions. In matrix-sensing experiments, the method reduces paired sensitivity by 18-29 percent for isotropic operators and 87-89 percent for weak-tail operators, without degrading reconstruction accuracy. These results demonstrate that parameter count alone does not determine robustness and identify solution geometry and the optimization trajectory as important levers for improving it.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在矩阵感知（可视为两层二次网络的训练）中研究 Burer-Monteiro 分解的过参数化与鲁棒性，提出秩感知的鲁棒性理论，说明敏感性同时取决于过参数化程度与二阶稳定点的局部几何，并提出用谱平衡与随机草图的轨迹感知算法把优化引向更不敏感的解。
AI.relevance_reason: 「解几何与优化轨迹共同决定敏感性、参数量本身不决定鲁棒性」的结论可能为 LVR 中 latent 表示的几何、过参数化与训练稳定性的关系提供类比线索，但领域相距较远，迁移可行性需要核查。
